import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from matplotlib.ticker import MaxNLocator

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: 'data/dogs_zurich.csv' not found.")
    print("Please make sure the dataset is in the 'data' directory.")
    # As a fallback for execution without the file, create a dummy dataframe
    data = {'StichtagDatJahr': [2020, 2021, 2022, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2020, 2021, 2022],
            'Rasse1Text': ['Labrador', 'Labrador', 'Labrador', 'Poodle', 'Poodle', 'Poodle', 'Mischling', 'Mischling', 'Mischling'],
            'AnzHunde': [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]}
    df = pd.DataFrame(data)


# --- Data Preparation ---
# Standardize breed names: strip whitespace and handle common cases
df['Rasse1Text'] = df['Rasse1Text'].str.strip().str.title()

# Identify the top 10 most frequent primary breeds across all years
top_10_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# Filter the dataframe to only include data for these top breeds
df_top_breeds = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_10_breeds)].copy()

# Ensure the breed column is treated as a categorical type with a specific order
# This ensures consistent coloring in the plot
df_top_breeds['Rasse1Text'] = pd.Categorical(df_top_breeds['Rasse1Text'], categories=top_10_breeds, ordered=True)

# Group by year and breed to get the annual count for each top breed
breed_trends = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'Rasse1Text']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
sns.set_context("talk")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 10))

# Create the line plot showing trends over time
sns.lineplot(
    data=breed_trends,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='count',
    hue='Rasse1Text',
    style='Rasse1Text',
    palette='tab10',
    markers=True,
    markersize=8,
    linewidth=2.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set title and labels with improved formatting
min_year = breed_trends['StichtagDatJahr'].min()
max_year = breed_trends['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
ax.set_title(
    f'Popularity Trends of Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich ({min_year}–{max_year})',
    fontsize=22,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=25
)
ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)

# Customize ticks and grid
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(integer=True)) # Ensure x-axis ticks are integers
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle='-', alpha=0.3)

# Enhance the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(
    handles=handles,
    labels=labels,
    title='Dog Breed',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=12,
    title_fontsize=14
)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
